label: Impulse!
rationale: Charlie Haden's debut as a bandleader, recorded April 27-29 1969 at Judson Hall, New York and released January 1970 on Impulse! (AS-9183). A political large-ensemble statement arranged by Carla Bley, weaving Spanish Civil War songs ('El Quinto Regimiento', 'Los Cuatro Generales', 'Viva la Quince Brigada'), Ornette Coleman's 'War Orphans', Haden originals ('Song for Ché', 'Circus '68 '69' — the latter re-enacting the 1968 Democratic Convention floor), and 'We Shall Overcome'. Personnel gravity is extraordinary: Don Cherry, Dewey Redman, Gato Barbieri, Roswell Rudd, Howard Johnson, Paul Motian, Andrew Cyrille. Consensus across the reception box: AllMusic 4.5 stars, DownBeat 4 stars (Dan Morgenstern), Penguin Guide 3.5 stars, Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide 5 stars; Lester Bangs in Rolling Stone called Bley's arrangements 'miracles of dynamics'. An opened-gate arrival (free jazz) — the council should weigh its continuity: the Ornette lineage (Haden had played 'War Orphans' with Coleman in 1967) and the JCOA-adjacent arranging tradition reach straight back into the post-bop canon, while the collective improvisation and political program mark the free-jazz boundary.

personnel_record.notes: Three-day session (April 27-29 1969) at Judson Hall, 165 West 57th Street, New York — the former Carl Fischer Concert Hall, renamed Judson Hall and reopened October 1960; new place minted. Released January 1970 on Impulse! AS-9183. Producer Bob Thiele per Wikipedia infobox; engineer not documented in the consulted sources (null, explicit). LP side A carries tracks 1-4 (The Introduction + Song of the United Front are printed together on the LP as one 3:07 track; the CD/iTunes sequence splits them, followed here since apple_album_id 1443906774 is the streaming copy). Don Cherry doubles on flute tracks 3 and 5 per Wikipedia numbering; Andrew Cyrille appears only on track 8. 'Circus '68 '69' divides the musicians into two bands re-enacting the 1968 Democratic Convention floor. Track-level personnel not assigned per-track (null); large-ensemble credits are album-level in the sources.

scope_check.boundary_note: Free-jazz gate (opened 2026-07-28) is in play; the album is a Bley-arranged large-ensemble political program that uses free-jazz vocabulary rather than pure energy music, so the bridge test is genuinely engaged rather than asserted

ballot.case_for: The bridge test is met head-on: Haden brings his Ornette Coleman lineage directly (Cherry and Redman on the date, 'War Orphans' in the book), Carla Bley's arranging reaches into the JCOA tradition, and the Spanish Civil War / 'We Shall Overcome' / 1968 DNC political program extends the Mingus line of politically engaged jazz — this is a load-bearing link between the post-bop center and the radical-political wing, not a free-jazz outlier. Session gravity is extraordinary: Cherry, Redman, Barbieri, Rudd, Howard Johnson, Mantler, Motian, Cyrille, Bley on one date. Cross-tradition consensus is real (AllMusic 4.5★, DownBeat 4★, Penguin 3.5★, Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide 5★; Lester Bangs called Bley's arrangements 'miracles of dynamics'), and it is the founding document of a project Haden returned to across five decades.
ballot.case_against: The free-jazz gate's standing taste note applies: John is still studying the idiom and the cull rate is high by design — 'Circus '68 '69,' which divides the band into two competing ensembles to re-enact the 1968 Democratic Convention floor, leans into the abrasive collective improvisation that is the hardest case in the project. The consensus ceiling is 'important and well-regarded,' not defining: no source places this alongside *The Shape of Jazz to Come* or *Out to Lunch!* at the top of the free-jazz sub-canon, and Penguin's 3.5★ is respectable but not a crown. Sourcing is effectively single-rooted in Wikipedia with AllMusic and Discogs as corroboration; track-level personnel is null, Cyrille's assignment is inferred from CD sequence, and the engineer is undocumented.
ballot.disagreement: Both references converge on contested/strong — no genuine split on tier or priority. Ref 1 emphasizes sourcing thinness and the consensus ceiling as the binding constraint; Ref 2 emphasizes 'Circus '68 '69' as the specific aesthetic-wall risk. The difference is emphasis, not outcome.
ballot.recommendation: The council proposes John hear the album end-to-end and rule on whether the folk-melody grounding carries the free-jazz vocabulary past his aesthetic wall — the bridge case is strong enough to warrant the listen, not strong enough to short-circuit it.
